key_insight: A flat plate reversing in its wake experiences excess drag from wake capture, and this interaction is governed mainly by how far it traveled before reversal.
engineering_relevance: For flapping and reciprocating actuators, wake history can materially change force predictions, so quasi-steady models need wake-state-aware corrections.
method: Translational forward-and-back motion of a flat plate at insect-flight-relevant Reynolds numbers
Measure drag during reversal and compare it with quasi-steady estimates
Interpret wake interaction using flow observations and a point-vortex model
evidence_signal: The abstract reports measured excess drag, two distinct wake-force peaks linked to vortex detachment/re-formation, and a scaling law tied to pre-reversal travel distance.
watch_item: The minimal point-vortex description captures scaling trends but may miss geometry-, viscosity-, and 3D-structure effects in real wings or actuators.
paper_title: Reversal of a flat plate into its wake: a minimal model for wake capture
